correctness.rationale: An endomorphism is uniquely (A,f,lambda) with A^tBA=lambda B and f arbitrary. A nonzero multiplier forces invertibility and contributes q^n times the similitude count. The multiplier image consists of squares in odd dimension by determinants and scalars, and all units in even dimension by hyperbolic-pair scaling and surjectivity of the norm on any anisotropic plane. At multiplier zero, choose an isotropic image U of dimension r and a surjection onto it; exactly q^r functionals vanish on the kernel, giving rank r, and the remaining functionals add one rank. For the polar factors, adding a hyperbolic plane gives the zero-vector-count recursion Z_(d+2)=(q-1)q^d+q Z_d, by counting solutions of xy=c, with base Z=1 in each anisotropic kernel of dimension 0, 1 or 2. The Z count includes the zero vector. Counting lines in r-spaces and passing to L-perp/L gives the claimed I products. Selecting a nonzero isotropic first vector, then a norm-zero partner with bilinear pairing 1, gives (Z_d-1)q^(d-2) choices of hyperbolic pair and reduces the isometry order to its dimension-(d-2) counterpart. The base orders are 1, 2 and 2(q+1), respectively. This also reconstructs the orthogonal group orders used. The rank support follows because every isotropic rank through the Witt index occurs and r<n. Summing over the functional fiber gives singular-stratum degree n+nr+r(n-2)-3r(r-1)/2, strictly increasing through w. The leading singular-minus-automorphism exponent is (m-1)(m+2)/2 for odd or split even, and (m^2-m-4)/2 for nonsplit even. Leading coefficients coincide in both ties (1 odd, 2 split), giving exactly the claimed threshold cases. At q=3,n=4 the isotropic counts are (1,16,8) split and (1,10) nonsplit; with P1=80, P2=6240 these reproduce both full example polynomials. Frozen code was inspected, not executed: direct histograms cover small n=2,3, with dimension 4 and 5 checks only of polar counts; the unrestricted proof does not rely on them.

value.rationale: This natural complete census explains how multiplication constrains ranks even when the map is not invertible. Its rank support detects the two Witt types and the density law separates small nonsplit spaces, a balanced regime and singular domination. These type-sensitive conclusions are not a recomputation of the isometry order or an arbitrary small-field slice.
